notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 95 this time. My one search attempt was rejected because the research tool said I had no searches or page reads left, so I didn't open a single source.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. A verse-by-verse set of notes written from memory would break all three, so I haven't written one.

**What I planned to read, once searching works again:**
- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** enduringword.com (Guzik on Psalm 95); biblehub.com and studylight.org (Gill, Ellicott, Barnes, Pulpit Commentary, Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*); preceptaustin.org.
- **Where traditions differ:**
  - Wesley's *Notes* (wesley.nnu.edu).
  - Reformed and Baptist teachers (ligonier.org, desiringgod.org, gty.org, spurgeon.org).
  - Lutheran sources (lcms.org, 1517.org).
  - The likely points of difference are on vv. 7b–11, which Hebrews 3–4 quotes: whether believers can fall away (Calvinist and Arminian views), and what the "rest" means, including Sabbath questions.
- **Other views:**
  - Modern scholarship: netbible.org notes on Meribah and Massah, the "forty years" and the oath, and bibleodyssey.org.
  - Catholic and Orthodox: Augustine's exposition at newadvent.org (in the Latin numbering this psalm is 94); catholic.com on the psalm's daily use at the start of morning prayer; oca.org.
  - Popular modern teaching (prosperity, word of faith, hyper-grace) only if these sites actually discuss it in connection with this psalm.

If you ask again in a new message, I should have searches available and can do the full research with a URL for every point.
